title: Local Authorization Is Not Operation
summary: A three-corridor map showing why market demand, permits, rate rules, environmental decisions, plans, and federal credit must pass through construction, acceptance, service, compliance, and measured operation.
map_question: Which records move a local system through authorization, and which downstream records are still needed before FTFN can claim operation or scale?
interpretation_boundary: The map compares evidence stages, not the technologies, markets, risks, or institutions themselves. A supported link shows a named record relationship, not project readiness.

nodes.label: Authorization and financing records
nodes.note: Rate decisions, permits, RODs, loans, site licenses, and plans establish different enabling stages.

nodes.label: Northern Virginia Data Center Corridor
nodes.note: Compute demand enters utility, transmission, water, permitting, and local acceptance systems.

nodes.label: Nevada Lithium And Battery Materials Corridor
nodes.note: Authorized projects must convert through water, finance, construction, compliance, qualification, and output.

nodes.label: Florida Space Coast Launch Corridor
nodes.note: Plans and site authorization must convert into accepted infrastructure, mission approval, safety, and utilization.

nodes.label: Construction and acceptance
nodes.note: Physical build, inspection, commissioning, acceptance, connection, and service records are required.

nodes.label: Measured operation and scale
nodes.note: Sustained load, output, mission activity, compliance, cost, reliability, safety, and local outcomes close the loop.

nodes.label: Northern Virginia delivery gap
nodes.note: Customer capacity, construction, energization, water, compliance, and local outcomes remain incomplete.

nodes.label: Nevada qualified-output gap
nodes.note: Construction, water, compliance, qualification, production, and repayment remain incomplete.

nodes.label: Space Coast license and delivery gap
nodes.note: Current SLF status, project acceptance, mission licensing, utilization, safety, and local outcomes remain incomplete.

links.note: SCC, county, DEQ, and provider records name corridor-specific rules and projects.
BLM, NDEP, DOE, and state water records name project authorization and finance stages.
NASA, FAA, FDOT, and Space Florida records name planning, licensing, environmental, and capital layers.
Golden-Mars and permit trails advance authorization, while final construction and service remain incomplete.
Thacker Pass has a closed loan and permits without a complete public acceptance and operating trail.
Plans, programs, site licenses, and environmental decisions require named project delivery records.
Accepted infrastructure still requires measured and sustained operating evidence.
Customer-specific delivery and local outcomes remain open.
Qualified and sustained material output remains open.
One license status and multiple project-to-operation layers remain open.

what_this_map_supports: The three corridors share an evidence-conversion problem even though their technologies and institutions differ.
Named authority records can be assigned to distinct stages rather than summarized as generic progress.
Construction, acceptance, service, compliance, operation, and scale require downstream records.
what_this_map_does_not_prove: That the three corridors are economically, environmentally, or institutionally equivalent.
That an authorization, loan, site license, or plan will produce a completed project.
That any corridor has spare capacity, qualified output, safe mission availability, or accepted local outcomes.
next_records_needed: Northern Virginia customer-service, route, construction, energization, water, and compliance records.
Nevada water, construction, commissioning, qualification, production, and loan-performance records.
Space Coast current license, capital-project, construction, acceptance, mission, utilization, and safety records.
